extracted.intended_audience: Users of the Magma computational algebra system (researchers and practitioners in computational group theory, algebraic geometry and combinatorics)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference/documentation for Magma functions and the mathematical criteria they implement, covering matrix group recognition, invariant computations, elliptic curve arithmetic and arithmetic invariants, and enumerative-combinatorics primitives. Explains required input conditions, semantics of return values, and computational caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classical group recognition (IsClassicalGroup / *Type / specific tests)
rubrics_metrics.description: IsClassicalGroup(G): true if S ≤ G ≤ Aut(S), where S is a classical group. Functions whose names end with Type determine whether, modulo scalars, G lies between a classical simple group and its automorphism group; other functions test whether G is a specific classical group or contains one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The functions employ Las Vegas algorithms. If any returns true, the answer is guaranteed correct; if false is returned the most that can be asserted is that G is probably not the group in question. IsClassicalGroup may also return the family name and, for symplectic/orthogonal/unitary cases, the preserved form.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsLinearGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: True if SL(d, q) ≤ G ≤ GL(d, q).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsSpecialLinearGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: True if G is the special linear group SL(n, q).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsSymplecticType
rubrics_metrics.description: True if G preserves a symplectic form up to scalar multiplication by a constant. In this case the form is also returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsSymplecticGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: True if G is the symplectic group Sp(n, q).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsOrthogonalType
rubrics_metrics.description: True if G preserves an orthogonal form (quadratic form for even characteristic) up to scalar multiplication by a constant. In this case the form is also returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsOrthogonalGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: True if either SO+(n, q) ≤ G ≤ GO+(n, q) or SO−(n, q) ≤ G ≤ GO−(n, q) for n even, or SO(n, q) ≤ G ≤ GO(n, q) for n odd.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsSpecialOrthogonalGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: True if G is either of the special orthogonal groups SO+(n, q) or SO−(n, q) for n even, or SO(n, q) for n odd.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsUnitaryType
rubrics_metrics.description: True if G preserves a unitary form up to scalar multiplication by a constant. In this case the form is also returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsUnitaryGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: True if SU(n, q) ≤ G ≤ GU(n, q).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsSpecialUnitaryGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: True if G is the special unitary group SU(n, q).

rubrics_metrics.name: Las Vegas algorithm correctness caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition functions use Las Vegas algorithms: true returns are guaranteed correct; false only indicates 'probably not'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should treat false negatives with caution and may need further checks. Successful true returns may include additional data (family name, preserved form).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aschbacher classification membership (categories i–ix)
rubrics_metrics.description: A finite matrix group G acting on KG-module V over finite field K satisfies at least one of the Aschbacher conditions: (i) reducible on V; (ii) semilinear over an extension field of K; (iii) imprimitivity on V; (iv) preserves nontrivial tensor-product decomposition; (v) has normal subgroup N acting absolutely irreducibly on V which is extra-special p-group or 2-group of symplectic type; (vi) preserves nontrivial symmetric tensor-product decomposition; (vii) acts (modulo scalars) linearly over a proper subfield of K; (viii) contains SL or a classical group in its natural action; (ix) almost simple.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Magma's functions aim to decide membership in at least one category and compute associated isomorphisms/decompositions. Groups in category (i) are recognised via Meataxe; category (viii) recognition has seen considerable progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix group reducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion (i): G acts reducibly on V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reducible groups can be recognised using Meataxe module-functions (see R-modules chapter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Semilinear over extension field
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion (ii): G acts semilinearly over an extension field of K (equivalently acts irreducibly but not absolutely irreducibly and can be rewritten as absolutely irreducible over extension L).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute irreducibility can be tested; if not absolute, consider redefining field to an extension L and reducing dimension over L.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imprimitivity on V
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion (iii): G acts imprimitively on V.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserves nontrivial tensor-product decomposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion (iv): G preserves a nontrivial tensor-product decomposition of V.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normal subgroup of extra-special/ symplectic type
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion (v): G has a normal subgroup N acting absolutely irreducibly on V which is an extra-special p-group or 2-group of symplectic type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserves symmetric tensor decomposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion (vi): G preserves a nontrivial symmetric tensor-product decomposition of V.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts linearly over proper subfield modulo scalars
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion (vii): G acts (modulo scalars) linearly over a proper subfield of K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contains special linear or classical group
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion (viii): G contains the special linear group, or one of the classical groups in its natural action over K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition of groups in this category has seen significant development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Almost simple groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion (ix): G is almost simple.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsInvariant (polynomial / element tests)
rubrics_metrics.description: IsInvariant(f, g): True iff polynomial f is an invariant of group element g. IsInvariant(f, G): True iff polynomial f is an invariant of group G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Molien series computation
rubrics_metrics.description: MolienSeries(G): The Molien series of group G, given as a rational function, which encodes dimensions of invariant spaces by degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Molien series is not available in the modular case (characteristic divides |G|). It is useful to determine possible degrees of primary invariants.

rubrics_metrics.name: MonomialsOfDegree
rubrics_metrics.description: MonomialsOfDegree(P, d): An indexed set containing all monomials of degree d from polynomial ring P.

rubrics_metrics.name: InvariantsOfDegree
rubrics_metrics.description: InvariantsOfDegree(G, d): A K-basis of the invariants of degree d of G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is also InvariantsOfDegree(G, d, k) returning k linearly independent invariants of degree d.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary and Secondary invariants
rubrics_metrics.description: PrimaryInvariants(G): A sequence of primary invariants of G. SecondaryInvariants(G): A sequence of secondary invariants of G (relative to chosen primaries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary invariants' degrees can be predicted by the Molien series in non-modular cases. Previous methods sometimes produced redundant primary sets leading to many secondaries; Magma's approach can produce compact sets. Secondary invariant computation may involve non-trivial Gröbner-basis elimination and benefits from the Hilbert-driven Buchberger algorithm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invariant ring construction
rubrics_metrics.description: InvariantRing(G): The invariant ring of G (generated by primary and secondary invariants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Elliptic curve definition criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: An elliptic curve over a field is a plane, non-singular cubic curve of genus 1 with a rational point; equivalently can be given in Weierstrass or extended Weierstrass form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-singularity is checked by ensuring the discriminant is non-zero. Over characteristics 2 or 3, extended Weierstrass form is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weierstrass / extended Weierstrass form constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard Weierstrass: Y^2 Z = X^3 + a X Z^2 + b Z^3. Extended form for char 2 or 3: Y^2Z + a1 XY Z + a3 Y Z^2 = X^3 + a2 X^2 Z + a4 X Z^2 + a6 Z^3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elliptic curves in Magma are defined by sequences of either 2 (short) or 5 (extended) Weierstrass coefficients coming from a field or ZZ (giving Q).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsEllipticCurve validity check
rubrics_metrics.description: IsEllipticCurve(coefs): Determines if the given coefficients define a non-singular elliptic curve; returns false and error if singular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use IsEllipticCurve to validate input before creating an EllipticCurve object; singular input triggers runtime error in EllipticCurve constructor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discriminant must be non-zero
rubrics_metrics.description: For a valid (non-singular) elliptic curve the discriminant is always non-zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discriminant(E) is used to detect singularity; BadPrimes etc. refer to discriminant of the minimal model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point creation / normalization rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Points on a curve are created by specifying 2 or 3 coordinates; if 2 are given z=1 is assumed and the point is normalized; the identity point O can be created by coercing 0 or Identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The group law uses '+'; inverse of (x:y:z) is (x:-y:z).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lift to extension fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Lift(E, F) creates a new elliptic curve by coercing coeﬃcients of E into field F; in Lift(E, M) a three-argument version allows explicitly specifying an embedding map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If coercion results in a singular curve in the target field, Lift fails with an error. Minimal models' lifts may succeed where original E does not (see BadPrimes warning).

rubrics_metrics.name: Isomorphism and integral/minimal models over Q
rubrics_metrics.description: Two curves are isomorphic over K if there exists a coordinate change x = u^2 x' + r, y = u^3 y' + s u^2 x' + t with r,s,t ∈ K and u ∈ K*. IntegralModel(E) returns an isomorphic curve with coefficients in ZZ. MinimalModel(E) returns the global minimal model M (minimising |Δ|) together with maps E→M and M→E. Reduced minimal model has a1,a3∈{0,1} and a2∈{-1,0,1} and is unique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discriminant scales by u^12; j-invariant unchanged. MinimalModel and IntegralModel are the recommended ways to obtain models with integer coefficients and minimal discriminant for arithmetic.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsIsomorphic test
rubrics_metrics.description: IsIsomorphic(E, F): returns true if curves E and F are isomorphic over Q; if true, returns the isomorphism map E→F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tate's algorithm outputs (local information)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given E and a prime p, Tate's algorithm produces local information tuple <p, e_p, f_p, c_p, k_p> where e_p = exponent of p in discriminant of minimal model M, f_p = exponent of p in conductor, c_p = Tamagawa number at p, k_p = Kodaira symbol classifying reduction type at p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use LocalInformation(E,p) or LocalInformation(E) to obtain tuples. Tate's algorithm itself is not described here (see reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tamagawa number definition
rubrics_metrics.description: c_p = [E(Q_p) : E^0(Q_p)], where E^0(Q_p) is subgroup of p-adic points whose reduction modulo p is non-singular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TamagawaNumber(E,p) retrieves cp for minimal model M.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kodaira symbol classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Kodaira symbol k_p classifies reduction type: I0 for good reduction (p does not divide Δ(M)); In (n>0) for bad multiplicative reduction; and n, II, II*, III, III*, IV or IV* for bad additive reduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KodairaSymbol(s) creates Kodaira symbols; KodairaSymbols(E) returns sequence for each bad prime. Special symbols 'In' and 'In*' compare equal to any In or In* respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: BadPrimes behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: BadPrimes(E) returns the sequence of primes dividing the discriminant of the minimal model M of E (not of E itself).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus lifting M into GF(p) is safe for those primes but lifting E might still fail if E is not defined over that residue field; use Lift(M, GF(p)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mordell-Weil group decomposition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Mordell-Weil group G = E(Q) is isomorphic to T × Z^r where T is finite torsion and r ≥ 0 is the rank. Torsion structure is constrained by Mazur's theorem (Ck for 1≤k≤10, C12, or C2k×C2 for 1≤k≤4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Magma provides functions to compute torsion subgroup, rank bounds, and (with heavier computation) the full group and generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: TorsionSubgroup behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: TorsionSubgroup(E) returns (i) an abelian group isomorphic to the torsion subgroup of E(Q) and (ii) a mapping from this group into E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computing torsion is comparatively straightforward; the returned mapping lets you view torsion elements as points on E.

rubrics_metrics.name: MordellWeilRank / Rank bounds
rubrics_metrics.description: MordellWeilRank(E) / Rank(E) returns the computed rank (a lower bound). MordellWeilRankBounds(E) / RankBounds(E) returns lower and upper bounds on the rank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rank computation uses descent methods (e.g., two-descent) and is not guaranteed to return exact rank; often bounds are returned. Rank is faster to compute than the full Mordell-Weil group; prefer Rank when sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: MordellWeilGroup (full group and generators)
rubrics_metrics.description: MordellWeilGroup(E) returns (i) an abelian group isomorphic to E(Q) and (ii) a mapping from this group into E; Generators(E) returns intrinsic generating points of E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computing the full group is the slowest operation: requires searching for generators up to bounds derived from heights and Silverman bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order(P) semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Order(P): returns the order of P in E(Q); returns 0 if P has infinite order; order of identity is 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heights and regulator functions
rubrics_metrics.description: NaiveHeight(P): log max{|m|,|n|} of x-coordinate m/n. LocalHeight(P,p): local canonical height at prime p (use p=0 for ∞). Height(P): canonical height ˆh(P) = Σ_p ˆh_p(P). HeightPairing(P,Q) = 1/2(ˆh(P+Q) − ˆh(P) − ˆh(Q)). Regulator(E) = |det(ˆh(Pi,Pj))| for a basis of the free part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Canonical heights and local heights are used to bound searches for generators. SilvermanBound(E) yields bounds on difference between naive and canonical heights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search strategy and computational caveats for generators
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute rank and bounds; use canonical heights of found subgroup generators to bound canonical heights of true generators via Silverman bounds; search for points up to the naive height bound. For most curves the bound grows quickly and search becomes infeasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer Rank or RankBounds when full generator search is infeasible. Generators returned by MordellWeilGroup come from this search and are not guaranteed feasible for very large bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting functions (enumerative combinatorics primitives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Elementary counting functions available: Factorial(n); NumberOfPermutations(n,k); Binomial(n,k); Multinomial(n,Q); Fibonacci(n); StirlingFirst(m,n); StirlingSecond(m,n); EulerianNumber(n,r); HarmonicNumber(n); BernoulliNumber(n); BernoulliApproximation(n); BernoulliPolynomial(n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions and conventions are provided (e.g., Fibonacci indexing, Stirling number interpretations). BernoulliApproximation returns a real approximation at current precision; BernoulliNumber returns rational exact value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsets / power-set semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsets(S) returns all subsets of an enumerated set S explicitly (as enumerated sets). PowerSet(S) returns a formal object representing the power set without enumerating elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Subsets(S,k) to get all k-subsets. Subsets(S) differs from PowerSet(S) by materializing elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multisets / Subsequences / Permutations semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Multisets(S,k) returns all k-multisets from S; Subsequences(S,k) returns all k-length sequences (ordered, with repetition allowed); Permutations(S,k) returns all k-permutations (ordered distinct-element sequences). Permutations(S) is special case with k = |S|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If k > |S| appropriate empty set is returned. Counting formulae: k-subsets = Binomial(n,k); k-multisets = Binomial(n+k-1,k); k-sequences = n^k; k-permutations = NumberOfPermutations(n,k).

rubrics_metrics.name: Partitions and restricted partitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Partitions(n) returns sequence of all partitions of integer n, each given as a non-increasing sequence. NumberOfPartitions(n) returns count. RestrictedPartitions(n,T) returns partitions whose parts lie in set T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partitions are classical integer partitions; RestrictedPartitions useful for coin-change and restricted-composition problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bell number computations (example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bell numbers B_n (number of partitions of an n-element set) can be computed via formulas involving Stirling numbers of the second kind: B_0 = 1; B_n = Σ_{k=1..n} S(n,k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple formulae/implementations exist with varying efficiency; examples demonstrate techniques: counting functions, summation, recursion, generating functions, approximations.
